title: CCI Quick Grant
who: Any artist living full-time in California
what: Up to $600 for workshops, conference or festival registration, a coach or consultant, memberships, travel, and the childcare you need to attend. Applications open on the 16th of each month and close on the 15th at 11:59 a.m. PT; you hear back by the 16th of the following month.

title: Theatre Bay Area CA$H grants
who: Individual theatre artists and small theatre companies in the Bay Area
what: $2,500 (CA$H Creates) or $5,000 (CA$H Performs). Companies must have budgets under $100,000. No extensions. The fall 2026 round closed Nov 2; watch the page for the next cycle.

title: Kala Art Institute Fellowship
who: Artists in any medium, local or not
what: $3,000 plus a one- to nine-month studio residency at Kala in Berkeley, a class or workshop, and a group show. Applications open December 2026 for the July 2027 to June 2028 residency year.
cost: Application fee not stated on the page; check before applying

title: Theatre Bay Area General Auditions 2027
who: Actors, union and non-union, with a free TBA individual membership
what: Live auditions Feb 6 and 7, 2027 at A.C.T.'s Strand Theater in San Francisco, in front of Bay Area theatre companies. Slots are limited; apply by Nov 19.

title: Bay Area makerspaces (Eddie's List)
who: Anyone who needs tools, a shop, or a workbench
what: A running list of makerspaces, library tool programs, and shared workshops around the Bay.

title: CCSF Free City
who: San Francisco residents taking credit classes at City College
what: Covers the $46-per-unit enrollment fee for any course of study: jewelry, film, acting, music, and more. Other small fees (health, registration, materials) still apply.

title: Discover & Go (SF Public Library)
who: San Francisco residents with a library card
what: Reserve free passes to museums, science centers, theaters, and other venues through the library. Two active reservations at a time; new passes release on the 1st of each month.

title: Beginner Bay Area Street Dance Resource Guide
who: Anyone curious about street dance
what: Decentered Arts' guide to classes, sessions, and community for people starting out in street dance in the Bay.

title: Renaissance Entrepreneurship Center
who: Artists running or starting a small business
what: Small-business training and support with San Francisco locations in SoMa and the Bayview. Recommended in the room by Sharon Zimmerman for individual classes.

title: Decentered's Bay Area Survival Guide
who: Artists getting by in the Bay
what: Decentered Arts' guide to resources for making it work here, shared at the October meetup.

title: Sharon Z Consulting: business advising for artists
who: Makers and artists who want help running the business side
what: Individual consulting from Sharon Zimmerman, a jewelry artist and business coach. At the October meetup she mentioned group classes (around 20 to 25 people, such as networking) are under consideration.

title: Decentered Event Tracker
who: Anyone looking for indie art events, or listing one
what: A community calendar of independent art events around the Bay, run by Decentered Arts.

title: Open Ballot: compare voter guides
who: California voters
what: Compare endorsements across voter guides side by side for the Nov 3, 2026 California general election.

title: Hospitality House Community Arts Program
who: Low-income SF artists and Tenderloin neighbors
what: Free fine-arts studio and gallery at 1009 Market St, with free materials. Artists keep 100% of sales. Open studio hours are posted on the site; call 415-553-4525 ext. 301 to confirm before your first visit.

title: Harvey Milk Photo Center
who: Photographers at any level
what: Public black-and-white darkroom with 30+ stations, film lab, digital lab, and classes. One-time $15 orientation, then a $25 day pass or a six-month membership ($88 limited, $221 unlimited). Classes don't require membership.

title: Oakland Tool Lending Library
who: Oakland, Piedmont, and Emeryville residents 18+
what: Borrow tools for seven days through Oakland Public Library. Register in person; reserve by phone at 510-597-5089.
cost: Free to borrow; late fees apply

title: SOMArts Ramp Gallery: open application
who: Bay Area artists, solo or group
what: Rolling applications for four-week shows in SOMArts' Ramp Gallery. Apply through the Google Form on the page.

title: CounterPulse Co-Produce
who: Performing artists with a finished work to stage
what: Subsidized space, marketing, and production support in CounterPulse's fall and spring seasons. Co-producers keep 100% of net ticket income. Rolling applications.

title: SF Art Vendor License
who: Artists and crafters who make their own work
what: A city license to sell original handmade work at designated street spots. Work is screened at a public committee meeting; spaces go by lottery or first come, first served.

title: Creative Capital Artist Lab
who: Individual artists, all disciplines
what: Free on-demand courses on grant writing, taxes, legal basics, insurance, and finances, plus live webinars. The courses are moving to a new site starting November 2026, so some may be briefly unavailable.

title: SF Office of Small Business: free counseling
who: Anyone running a small business in SF, including a sole-proprietor art practice
what: Free one-on-one counseling, permit help, webinars, and trainings from the city's small-business office and SBDC advisers.

title: Covered California open enrollment
who: Uninsured Californians
what: Open enrollment for 2027 health plans runs Nov 1 to Jan 31. Enroll by Dec 31 for coverage starting Jan 1; most people qualify for financial help.

title: Healthy San Francisco
who: Uninsured SF residents 18+ not eligible for Medi-Cal or Medicare, income up to 500% of the poverty level
what: The city's health-access program for uninsured adults. Immigration status and pre-existing conditions don't bar enrollment. Enroll through a Certified Application Assistor.

title: Artists' Fellowship emergency aid
who: Professional visual artists in a recent, unexpected emergency
what: One-time aid for illness, disaster, bereavement, or serious emergency. Average award $2,500, up to $20,000. Requires two complete recent federal tax returns; a Schedule C helps show a working practice, and you can explain in your letter if you don't have one. The board meets monthly, September through June.

title: SF Artist Housing Certification
who: SF artists, by income, grant history, or portfolio
what: A certification that gives lottery priority for the Artists Hub on Market affordable artist housing. The portfolio pathway needs no income or grant history. Applications aren't open yet; the city expects the housing lottery in late 2027. Check the page for when certification opens.

title: Intersection for the Arts fiscal sponsorship
who: Bay Area artists and project directors who need a nonprofit umbrella to receive grants and tax-deductible gifts
what: Rolling applications, reviewed and onboarded in cohorts. Basic: $100 a year plus 9% of funds raised. Comprehensive: $150 a year plus 11%. The page lists the next cohort deadline as Jan 31, 2027, with applications reopening Dec 1, 2026; email fiscalsponsorship@theintersection.org to confirm timing.

title: SF Arts Commission individual artist grants (FY2028)
who: SF artists
what: The city says FY2028 grant programs are not yet available and details are expected later this fall (2026). Past cycles have funded individual artists.

title: City of Berkeley Individual Artist Projects grant
who: Berkeley residents
what: Project grants for Berkeley-resident artists. FY28 deadlines will be released in fall 2026; the city anticipates the application window Jan–Mar 2027.

title: Headlands Center for the Arts residencies (2028)
who: Artists in all disciplines
what: The 2027 cycle is closed; the 2028 application opens April 2027.

title: SFFILM filmmaker funds (2027 cycles)
who: Filmmakers
what: SFFILM's Rainin, Documentary, and Cedar Road funds are closed for 2026. Watch the page for the 2027 cycles.

title: Free tax help (VITA partner sites)
who: SF residents with household income up to $67,000
what: Free tax preparation through city partners. The page still shows the 2025-return season; the next season's dates aren't posted yet.

title: Field Funds: Artist-led Gatherings (A Blade of Grass)
who: US-based artists with a history of socially engaged work; nonprofits and businesses can't apply
what: $500 for a gathering of three or more people, in person or online, public or private, spent however you see fit. Eligible applications are picked at random, so there's no pitch to win; 5–7 are funded this cycle. Applications close Nov 30 at 8:59 p.m. PT (11:59 p.m. ET). Funded gatherings happen Dec 16, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Drop-in Zoom office hours Nov 16 (10–11 a.m. PT) and Nov 23 (12–1 p.m. PT).

title: Artist Space Trust: Celadon House (Mission District)
who: Artist households of 2 to 7 people, first-time buyers, with household income at or below 80% of area median (for example $134,500 for two people)
what: A 3-bedroom Mission District home sold for $425,000 through a community land trust, with up to $100,000 in down-payment help. At least one adult must have an active art practice; AST doesn't judge the work. You'll need an 8-hour homebuyer course and a mortgage through Habitat for Humanity Greater SF. Living or working in SF, or a Mission connection, gets lottery preference.

title: World Arts West Grant Accelerator (2027 cohort)
who: Bay Area cultural artists and organizations historically excluded from philanthropy
what: A free year-long cohort: eleven 90-minute sessions (third Wednesday mornings, Jan to Dec 2027) plus a monthly 30-minute one-on-one with a grant specialist. You commit to submitting at least three grant applications during the year.

title: Marin Cultural Association: Arts Across Marin grants
who: Individual artists, artist collectives, nonprofits, and fiscally sponsored groups with a project in Marin County
what: $10,000 project grants (about five this round) for work that happens in a Marin supervisorial district between May 1, 2027 and April 30, 2028; funds can cover materials, honoraria, production, and other project costs. Closes Dec 4 at 5 p.m. A recorded info session is on the page and you can book a free community meeting to ask questions.

title: Svane Family Foundation: Culture Forward
who: Individual artists, collectives, and arts organizations with a project in downtown San Francisco (Tenderloin, SoMa, Mid-Market, Chinatown, Civic Center, Union Square, Mission Bay, Financial District)
what: Project grants, typically $10,000 and up, for arts and culture that draws families, students, and young professionals downtown. Individuals and collectives apply through a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor. Rolling applications reviewed quarterly; the site lists Dec 1 as the next cutoff.

title: Zellerbach Community Arts grants
who: Emerging artists and small to mid-sized arts groups in San Francisco, Alameda, and Contra Costa counties
what: $5,000, $10,000, or $15,000 for projects that bring art to Bay Area communities. Individual artists apply through a fiscal sponsor (see Intersection for the Arts). Due dates run quarterly: Jan 21, Apr 22, Jul 15, and Oct 14, 2027, with notice about 11 weeks later.

title: Foundation for Contemporary Arts Emergency Grants
who: Visual and performing artists and poets anywhere in the US
what: $500 to $3,000 (average about $2,200) when you have a sudden chance to present work and no time to raise money, or unbudgeted costs on a nearly finished project with a confirmed show date. Reviewed year-round; roughly 15 to 20 grants a month.

title: Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants (NYFA)
who: Visual artists, film/video and digital artists, and choreographers, 21+, living in the US, with income under about $80,000
what: One-time grants up to $5,000 for a recent, unexpected medical, dental, or mental health emergency. Cycles open every two months; Cycle 39 closes Nov 17, 2026 at 5 p.m. ET, and the next cycle should open in December.

title: California Arts Council Individual Artist Fellowships (via Kala)
who: Artists of any discipline in Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, or Sonoma counties
what: $5,000 (emerging), $10,000 (established), or $50,000 (legacy). Kala Art Institute runs the Bay Area round; the 2026 window was Apr 2 to Jun 5.

title: Southern Exposure: Alternative Exposure
who: Bay Area and Santa Cruz County artists organizing public visual art programs outside traditional art spaces
what: Up to $5,000 to seed artist-led exhibitions, publications, festivals, screenings, and more that present work by multiple artists. Round 20 closed Aug 17, 2026.

title: Community Engagement: Artists & Creatives Grants
who: Independent artists and collectives making community-engaged work; the spring round is open nationwide, the fall round is California only
what: Generally up to $2,500, with encouragement for artists historically excluded from the mainstream art world. Spring deadline is in March; fall deadline is in September.

title: Recology SF Artist in Residence (2028)
who: Bay Area artists living within an hour's drive of the SF Transfer Station
what: Six professional residencies a year, four months each, in a studio at Recology's San Francisco site. Applications for 2028 open Jun 1 to Sep 1, 2027; you must take a site tour first.

title: ARTogether Mini-Grants for Artists
who: Bay Area refugee and immigrant artists with a current project
what: $500 for supplies, equipment, costumes, or professional help like editing. Rolling when open; applications are closed right now. One grant per artist.
